artifact.title: Personas
artifact.question: Who are we designing for, what do they do all day and where do they stand on handing work to an agent?
artifact.iDecided: Four composites cut by accountability, not by seniority alone, plus one anti-persona. Role-based views of the same run came out of this cut.
artifact.weBuilt: The cards from the coded material, with the evidence rows attached, reviewed in critique by the whole design team.

label: Composite and reconstructed. Each persona is a composite built from the themes in 03. No attribute carries an observation, participant or quote count. Names are invented.

personas.name: Dana Whitlock
personas.tenure: Fourth busy season. Runs fieldwork on three engagements at once.
personas.environment: Client site three days a week, laptop on a shared table, calls interrupting. Firm office or home the other two.
goals: Get every sample traced and every exception explained before the manager's review slot.
Hand the manager a file that needs no re-walk.
Keep the associates moving without redoing their work.
tasks: Design the sample and assign items.
Trace samples to evidence, clear the hard ones herself.
Raise and resolve exceptions with the client.
Draft conclusions and prepare for review.
tools: Email and chat with the client
personas.expertise: Knows the procedure cold. Knows which client contact answers which request. Does not need guidance; needs speed.
frustrations: Three systems opened to find one statement.
Re-walking the sample for the manager because the file does not hold the state.
personas.pressure: Owns the fieldwork result. If the file is late or thin, it is her name the manager says first.

ai.handoff: Retrieval, extraction and the field-by-field matching. 'It can do the matching. I will look at the differences.'
ai.never: Deciding what an exception means. Talking to the client about it.
ai.trust: Seeing the page it read, next to the field it extracted. Being able to rerun one step with the right file.

personas.name: Rafael Osei
personas.tenure: Eight years. Reviews for five engagements in the same weeks.
personas.environment: Mostly office or home. Review happens in blocks between client meetings, often late.
goals: Clear review queues before the partner needs the file.
Catch the reference and format problems early so they do not reach the partner.
Know, at a glance, what is waiting on whom.
tasks: Decide what escalates to the partner.
tools: Email for notes outside the system
A personal list of what is waiting
personas.expertise: Reads a workpaper by its references first. Knows which seniors need a second look.
frustrations: Layout differs per team, so decoding precedes judging.
No view of the whole queue across engagements.
personas.pressure: Signs the review. Shares the consequence of anything the partner finds later.

ai.handoff: Drafting with references in place. Flagging exceptions with the evidence attached.
ai.never: The review decision itself. 'A number alone is not confidence.'
ai.trust: Step-level visibility. Rejecting one step without discarding the run. Knowing the agent could not read restricted material without a checkpoint.

personas.name: Ingrid Haller
personas.tenure: Nineteen years. Signs for a portfolio of engagements.
personas.environment: Travelling between clients. Reads on a laptop in short windows. Signs when the file is ready, not when it is convenient.
goals: Sign a file she could defend to an inspector a year later.
See the exception trail before the conclusion.
Spend her attention on judgment, not on format.
personas.expertise: Pattern-matches across engagements. Knows which exceptions become findings.
frustrations: The exception trail is spread across workpapers and emails.
Being asked to sign before the review is complete.
Not knowing what a tool did with the client's data.
personas.pressure: Personal liability. Independence. 'If it is wrong, it is still my name.'

ai.handoff: Assembly of the evidence trail. Consistency checks across workpapers.
ai.never: Conclusions. Sign-off. Anything that writes into the file as final.
ai.trust: A human checkpoint before anything restricted was read. A visible record of what the agent did, in the file, not in a log.

personas.name: Tomasz Brenner
personas.tenure: Twelve years in audit, four in methodology.
personas.environment: Firm office. Works across engagements, not inside one. Writes the rules teams work to.
goals: Rules that teams can follow without memorizing them.
Structures that fit procedures so teams stop adapting them by hand.
A file that can be re-performed from its contents.
tasks: Maintain the Test of Details structures.
personas.expertise: Knows every structure and why each field exists. Knows where teams deviate and what it costs.
frustrations: Reviewing rules in documents nobody reads under pressure.
personas.pressure: Answers for methodology compliance across the practice.

ai.handoff: Planning a run against a typed structure. Enforcing data classes. Documenting steps consistently.
ai.never: Changing a structure or a rule without methodology review.
ai.trust: The agent plans against the library, not around it. Checkpoints are rules in the product, not guidance in a document.

anti.name: Caleb Marsh
anti.label: Anti-persona: the auditor who routes around the tool
anti.who: Fast, competent, keeps a personal tracker because the systems never held the state he needed. Trusts his own spreadsheet over any tool that slows him down or hides what it did.
why: Any step that adds a click without adding certainty.
Any output he cannot check in seconds.
Any tool that makes the risk his while keeping the work invisible.
signals: Copies data out to a spreadsheet.
Approves agent output without opening the source.
Reruns the whole run instead of fixing one step.
design_response: Keyboard-first density so the product is faster than the spreadsheet (D-15).
Citation chips that make checking faster than trusting (D-03).
Step-level rejection and rerun so fixing is cheaper than discarding (D-14).
The run holds the state he used to keep in his head (D-13).
